Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 July 1979, after the draft finalized by the Dye Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 Cyanuric chloride ( C&N&la ) is an important intermediate used in It is also used in the manufacture of the manufacture of reactive dyes. fluorescent brightening agents and herbicides. It is represented by the following structural formula:

Add 40 ml of sodium hydroxide ( 1 N ) solution and Immerse the flask in a water bath maintained at about stopper the flask. 50�C and shake it gently until all the crystals of cyanuric chloride are Cool and titrate against sulphuric acid ( 1 N ) using phenoldissolved. phthalein as the indicator.
A-2.2.2 Weigh another `2 g of the same material into a separating funnel of 200 ml capacity. Add 30 ml of benzene and shake well to dissolve. Then add 100 ml of ice-cold water and shake well. Allow the lavers to separate. Draw out the aqueous layer completely and filter it. Wash the filter with ice-cold water. Collect the filtrate and washings.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 MAY 2002 TO IS 9288:1979 SPECIFICATION FOR CYANURIC CHLORIDE
( Page 4, clause 2.2) -- Insert the following new clause atler 2.2:

2.3 Particle Size -- Not more than 2.0 percent by mass of the material shall be retained on 250 micron IS Sieve [ IS 460 (F%@ 1) :1985 ] and not more than 8.0 percent by mass of material shall be retained on 150 micron IS Sieve when tested in accordance with method given in A-5. ( Page 8, clause A-4.1.1) -- Insert the following new clause after A-4.1.1: A-5 PARTICLE SIZE Transfer 25.0 g of the sample to the designated sieve and replace the lid. Start sieving gently by banging on a pad of latex foam or similar material. Brush the residue gently with a camel hair brush to ensure that any remaining soft aggregates are broken down, calculate and report the percentage retained on each sieve.
NOTE -- Safety precaution as detaiied for Wis test must be followed strictly. The test must be carried out in a fuming cupboard and robber gloves, respirator and ptsatic apron must be worn. Base and sides of fuming cupboard must he lined with paper before commencing the test. After completion of test transfer residue and the material passing through the sieves to a beaker containing about 1.5 liSre of 10 percent sodium hydroxide solution. Mix well and allow to stand overnight in the fuming cupboard. I%salty pour down the waste in sink followed by flow of cold water. W@c the lining paper with a cloth soaked in 10 percent sodium hydroxide solution and screw up the paper in an outside dust b.

A-5.1 Calculation % Retained on 250 micron sieve where X = g of sample retained on 250 micron sieve and % Retained on 150 micron sieve where X= g of sample retained on 250 micron sieve, and Y= g of sample retained on 150 micron sieve. (PCD1l)
